name: Autoencoders
description: Autoencoders are neural networks trained to copy their input to their output through a compressed representation (bottleneck). The architecture consists of an encoder that compresses data to a latent representation and a decoder that reconstructs the original input. Used for dimensionality reduction, denoising, and feature learning.

architecture.encoder: Maps input x to latent representation z = f(x)
architecture.decoder: Reconstructs input x̂ = g(z) from latent representation

concept.undercomplete: Bottleneck smaller than input forces learning useful representations
concept.overcomplete: Bottleneck larger or equal; needs regularization to learn
concept.explanation: By forcing data through a bottleneck, autoencoders learn to capture most important aspects of data for reconstruction.

latentDim.impact: Smaller = more compression, risk of information loss

lossFunction.impact: MSE for continuous, BCE for binary/normalized data

regularization.impact: Prevents overfitting, especially in overcomplete autoencoders

architectureDesign: Tied weights (decoder uses encoder weights transposed) optional
training: Feed input through encoder → bottleneck → decoder
Use validation set for early stopping
usage: Encoder for dimensionality reduction (extract latent features)

complexity.timeTraining: O(epochs × n × params) like other neural nets
complexity.interpretability: Low - latent features learned, not designed

pros: Flexible architecture (can use CNN for images)
Useful for denoising and anomaly detection
cons: Risk of learning identity function (trivial solution)

variants.denoising: Train on corrupted input, reconstruct clean
variants.sparse: Add sparsity constraint on latent representation
variants.contractive: Penalize sensitivity of latent to input changes
variants.convolutional: Use CNN layers for image data
